# Ref_Exchange__Shipped Playbook

## Trading Phase

When making an offer, calculate exactly what resources I need to complete a build this round. Identify which opponent has surplus resources I need, and offer one of my surplus resources in return.

When I have a clear path to build a valuable structure (settlement > road), prioritize getting those exact resources through trade rather than holding back.

Do not post offers unless I can realistically complete a settlement this round. Rejected offers waste no resources, but offering suboptimal or unfavorable terms signals weakness and may not even be accepted.

In the final round, if I'm tied or ahead, avoid trading to strengthen opponents. A trade that helps me reach a settlement is worth it; a trade that merely helps an opponent is not.

## Accept Phase

When I already have all resources needed for a settlement this round, reject all incoming offers. Accept trades only if they move me closer to a settlement I couldn't otherwise build.

## Building Phase

When I can afford a settlement, build it. Settlements are worth 3 points; roads are worth 1 point. The point differential is too large to justify building roads when settlements are available.

When I have exactly the resources for a settlement (1 of each resource type), take that settlement. Do not wait for future rounds hoping for better circumstances.

When I cannot build anything due to missing resources, post none and accept the zero-point round rather than wasting resources on suboptimal builds.

## General Strategy

Prioritize building settlements early. Each settlement is 3 points, and early settlements build momentum and a lead that becomes difficult to overcome.

Always verify I have all four required resources (wood, brick, grain, ore) before committing to a settlement build. Avoid the trap of thinking I'm "close" to a settlement when I'm actually missing a critical resource.

In mid-game rounds, be willing to trade away one of my two abundant resources to secure a settlement. This trade-for-settlement strategy is worth the resource exchange, but only if the trade actually secures a settlement I can build.

Track opponent point totals. In the final round, if I have a lead, protect it by avoiding trades that help opponents catch up—unless the trade is essential to building my own settlement and winning outright.

Be realistic about trade acceptance. If an opponent won't accept an offer (especially P1 with scarce ore), don't post it. Save posting offers for trades that are genuinely attractive to both sides.

# Playbook for ref_exchange__shipped

## Trading Phase Strategy

When I post an offer, I should focus on completing resource sets that let me build immediately, not just improve flexibility. Target trades that get me to a settlement (1 of each resource) within one round if possible.

When I receive an offer, evaluate it against my immediate build potential. Don't accept trades just because they improve "balance"—accept only if they move me closer to a buildable state or if I'm ahead and can afford to help opponents less than they help me.

In the final round, don't trade away resources unless the trade directly enables a build I couldn't otherwise make. Resource conversion for its own sake wastes a turn.

## Building Phase Strategy

Always build a settlement when I can afford it (3 points is significantly better than a road's 1 point). Build roads only when I cannot build a settlement and building is still advantageous—in the final round, a road is better than nothing, but in earlier rounds, sometimes saving resources for better opportunities matters more.

## Resource Tracking and Scarcity

Pay close attention to which resources other players have and which are scarce across the table. If all players are low on wood, wood will be hard to trade for. Mid-game, I accumulated grain and brick but lost access to wood early. In endgames with low wood availability, I cannot build roads or settlements that require it.

Actively work to diversify my resource holdings in early-to-mid rounds so I'm not locked into a single resource type by the final rounds.

## Game Positioning

Watch what other players are building and their point totals. If I'm behind by more than I can realistically close, don't waste resources on marginal trades trying to catch up. If I'm competitive, identify which resources I need and pursue them directly.

Recognize when I'm in an endgame (final round especially) and stop speculating. Either I have the resources to build something that scores, or I don't. Accept that constraint rather than hoping for trades that probably won't happen.

## What Didn't Work

I traded away brick for grain mid-game based on the idea of "improving balance," then found myself unable to build settlements later due to missing wood entirely. By round 5, I had no wood and couldn't build anything despite having 4 brick and 5 grain—the only resource that mattered was the one I lacked.

Be more specific: only trade for resources I actually need to complete a build in the near term, and actively maintain some minimum of each critical resource (especially wood, needed for both roads and settlements). A surplus of one resource is only useful if I can trade it for what I actually lack.

# Playbook for ref_exchange__shipped

**On resource scarcity and trading:**
When I lack a critical resource for my next build, immediately identify which opponent has it and propose a trade. Don't wait passively hoping resources will be yielded to me—the game is short (5 rounds) and passive play leaves me behind. Target the player most willing to trade rather than the most abundant holder if they're the same person.

**On accepting trades:**
When offered a trade that improves my resource diversity without crippling any future build path, accept it. Ore and brick tend to be bottleneck resources; trading abundant resources (like my extra wood or grain) for scarce ones is usually sound. Accept early if the offer is fair.

**On building settlements:**
A settlement is +3 points and costs 1 of each resource. Roads are +1 point. Prioritize settlements heavily—they're the primary way to score in this game. Build them whenever I can assemble 1 wood, 1 brick, 1 grain, 1 ore. In round 1, if I have a balanced hand and can reach a settlement with a single trade, execute that trade immediately and build.

**On the brick bottleneck:**
Brick appears to be the resource I'm most likely to run short on. In early rounds, if I have decent brick reserves, I should protect them and not trade them away unless getting something equally scarce in return. In later rounds when I'm behind on points, be willing to trade for brick at a premium if needed to build.

**On resource burn and the resource pipeline:**
This game punishes active builders who spend resources faster than they can replenish them. I must maintain a sustainable cycle: build only when I'm confident the yields and trades in the coming rounds will restock me for the next build. If I build a settlement in round 1, I immediately enter a debt state (0 ore, reduced wood/brick). I must have a clear plan for how I'll acquire all four resources again by round 2 or 3, or I'll spiral into the locked-out state I reached in this game. Trading away a resource to enable one build is only sound if I have a realistic pipeline to replenish all four resources within 1-2 rounds afterward.

**On the perils of unbalanced trades:**
A trade that looks good in isolation can destroy my position if it breaks my resource symmetry. In this game, I gave up grain early (abundant for me) but then couldn't rebuild it because yields and counterparties both failed me. Before accepting any trade, simulate the next 2-3 rounds: Can I rebuild this resource? Will the yields support it? If the answer is "I'm betting on a specific opponent's yield or a specific trade that might not happen," don't make it.

**What failed this game:**
I built a settlement in round 1 correctly, but then failed to secure a sustainable resource pipeline. Yields were insufficient; I couldn't rebuild my stock fast enough. By round 2, I was already one resource short of another settlement, and the trades available to me didn't lead anywhere. I compounded this by making isolated trades (ore for grain) without a multi-round plan. By round 4, I had zero resources and couldn't build. The root cause: I didn't assess whether the game's resource yields and available counterparties could support repeated settlement building. I should have either built fewer settlements or secured explicit multi-round trade agreements earlier.

**On final rounds:**
If I'm substantially behind in points with only 1-2 rounds left and I lack critical resources with no way to rebuild, I'm already lost. Don't waste offers trying to recover at that stage. Instead, by round 2-3, assess whether I'm on a sustainable settlement-building trajectory. If not, pivot earlier rather than wait until round 4. A single settlement in round 1 followed by resource starvation is worse than building roads steadily or securing a resource pipeline that enables repeated settlements.

**On reading the board state:**
Before I post an offer, I must verify that the counterparty actually has the resource I'm asking for *and* that accepting my offer doesn't leave me unable to build next round. Don't assume trades will happen or that yields will bail me out. Map out the minimum resources I need to stay alive (hold the 4 resources or a clear path to them), then trade the surplus only.
